text:
Anton Lundell has two Stanley Cup rings at 25 and a job description that doesn't fill a highlight reel: take the hard matchups and keep the puck moving the right way. Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 90th percentile last season, and this year the Panthers control 54.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, 5.2 points better than without him.

The scoring line hasn't caught up. He has 13 points in 24 games, below the 44-point pace of last season, but his own finishing is fine (8 goals on 7.6 expected). The gap is around him: Florida has scored 5.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Lundell on the ice, and that has cost him assists. That kind of shortfall usually evens out.

He's shooting more, too: 62 shots in 24 games, a career-heavy rate for him. The last ten games brought 4 goals and 7 points. If the teammates' finishing turns, the point total should follow the play.
